title: One mass, several dependent scale representations
question: Which particle scales follow from invariant mass, and which require a momentum state?
answerPreview: Rest energy and Compton wavelength follow from invariant mass; de Broglie wavelength follows from the selected state momentum, so linked displays are dependencies rather than independent measurements.
summary: Compare electron, muon, proton, and neutron scales while separating catalog mass, mass-derived rest and Compton representations, and state-dependent momentum and de Broglie wavelength.

observationStage.title: Catalog masses are the shared inputs
observationStage.question: How many independent quantities are present when one mass is shown on linked energy and wavelength axes using International System of Units (SI) values?

items.label: Electron rest mass
items.explanation: The CODATA adjusted invariant mass is the catalog input from which this activity derives electron rest energy and Compton scales.

items.label: Proton rest mass
items.explanation: The proton catalog mass describes a composite particle; the activity does not infer its internal mass decomposition.

items.label: Speed of light in vacuum
items.explanation: The SI fixes c exactly. It maps a selected massive-particle rest mass to rest energy and a chosen m c momentum scale.

observationStage.conclusion: The linked energy and Compton axes are deterministic representations of one selected catalog mass and fixed constants. Momentum and de Broglie wavelength add a declared state dependency, not another mass measurement.

attribution.sourceLocator: Particle masses and exact h and c
caveats: Dependency labels do not constitute uncertainty propagation or covariance analysis.

guidedBlocks.title: Rest energy and Compton scale share one cause
body: For a selected massive particle, E_0 = m c^2 expresses its rest energy and lambda_C = h/(m c) expresses its Compton wavelength.
Both are derived from the same catalog invariant mass and fixed constants. Showing joules and electron volts, or ordinary and reduced Compton wavelengths, does not create independent observations.
A heavier selected mass gives a larger rest energy and a shorter Compton scale within these identities.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: CODATA 2022 masses; SI Brochure 2026 update; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27
guidedBlocks.sourceLocator: Mass-energy and Compton identities; OpenStax sections 5.9 and 6.3
caveats: The Compton wavelength is a characteristic mass scale, not a measured particle diameter.

guidedBlocks.title: de Broglie wavelength follows the state momentum
body: The de Broglie relation lambda_dB = h/p requires a positive momentum magnitude for the selected state. In this activity p is chosen as a multiplier of m c.
Changing momentum while holding particle mass fixed changes lambda_dB and relativistic total energy, but it does not change rest energy or the Compton wavelength.
Momentum is frame- and state-dependent; it is not another representation of invariant mass.

caveats: Direction, wave-packet spread, interactions, and localization are omitted.

guidedBlocks.title: A composite mass needs a different interpretation
body: The electron and muon are treated as elementary catalog entries in this bounded comparator. The proton and neutron are composite.
A proton or neutron invariant mass includes internal field and constituent dynamics; it is not the simple sum of freely measured constituent rest masses.
The same external free-particle identities can use a composite particle's total invariant mass without explaining its internal structure.
guidedBlocks.sourceLocator: Particle catalog composition and Chapter 8 limits
caveats: No constituent, binding-energy, or hadron-structure model is evaluated.

technicalBlocks.title: Relativistic energy separates invariant and state terms
body: The free-particle relation E^2 = (p c)^2 + (m c^2)^2 combines the invariant rest term with the selected momentum state.
At p = m c, E = sqrt(2) m c^2 and lambda_dB = lambda_C. This equality follows from the chosen state and does not identify the two concepts generally.
The engine computes kinetic energy as E - E_0 using an algebraically stable equivalent expression.

technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: Exact c; OpenStax sections 5.8-5.9; Chapter 8 technical extension
caveats: The relation is for a free particle in vacuum and omits interactions and finite width.

technicalBlocks.title: Track the dependency before comparing axes
body: Catalog dependency: invariant mass and composition label come from the bounded CODATA-backed catalog.
Mass-derived dependency: rest energy, mass ratios, Compton wavelength, and reduced Compton wavelength all reuse that mass.
State dependency: momentum, de Broglie wavelength, total energy, and kinetic energy additionally reuse the selected momentum state.
caveats: The dependency labels are provenance categories, not statistical independence tests.

equationSteps.label: Mass-derived representations
equationSteps.expression: E_0 = m c^2; lambda_C = h/(m c); reduced_lambda_C = hbar/(m c) = lambda_C/(2 pi)
equationSteps.explanation: All three outputs reuse one selected invariant mass; ordinary and reduced Compton scales differ by the explicit factor 2 pi.
equationSteps.sourceLocator: Particle masses and exact h, hbar, and c
caveats: These representations are not independent measurements or particle radii.

equationSteps.label: State-dependent wavelength
equationSteps.expression: p = k m c; lambda_dB = h/p = lambda_C/k
equationSteps.explanation: The control selects k between 10^-6 and 10^6, so de Broglie wavelength changes with state momentum while lambda_C stays mass-derived.
equationSteps.sourceLocator: Exact h and c; bounded momentum-state identity
caveats: The state uses a momentum magnitude and does not represent direction or spread.

equationSteps.label: Free-particle total energy
equationSteps.explanation: Total and kinetic energy depend on both invariant mass and the selected momentum state.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: SI Brochure 2026 update; conventional free-particle relation
equationSteps.sourceLocator: Exact c and free-particle dispersion relation
caveats: Potential energy and medium effects are absent.

checkpoints.prompt: If the selected particle stays the same and its momentum multiplier doubles, what happens?
checkpoints.explanation: lambda_dB = h/p halves when p doubles. The selected invariant mass and its Compton wavelength remain fixed.

caveats: This authored answer is not a learner result.
